slides.notes: Public design-partner opener. Keep the proposition intact and do not add deployment, customer, or readiness language.

elements.text: One inspectable decision thread
Start with a threat, control, requirement, component, supplier, test, or finding and follow the relevant evidence, derivation, uncertainty, and remaining human decision.
Why do we believe this?
What is missing, stale, disputed, or still only a candidate?
Who is allowed to decide?
What blocks signoff next?

slides.notes: Use native slide shapes for the decision-thread visual; do not paste the README's long workflow verbatim.

elements.text: The failure is not finding another document
The failure is carrying a defensible claim across frameworks, program records, suppliers, tests, review states, and decision owners without collapsing their authority.
General-purpose models remain fluent when evidence is weak.
Relevance is easily mistaken for evidentiary support.
Candidate mappings can look like approved compliance conclusions.
Teams rebuild the same decision thread across disconnected tools.

slides.notes: Frame the problem as evidence and authority fragmentation, not as a generic search or chatbot problem.

elements.text: Three boundaries make the product useful
The system is designed to make uncertainty and authority visible rather than turn navigation into approval.
Relevance is not support — retrieval identifies useful material but does not prove the claim.
Candidate visibility is not compliance credit — proposed mappings stay separate from reviewed conclusions.
A model may explain; a person still decides — approval, risk, certification, and signoff remain human authorities.

slides.notes: This is the deck's intellectual center. Preserve the three distinctions exactly enough that later slides cannot imply stronger authority.

elements.text: Shared foundation, separated authority
Plant and warfighter-program evidence can share governed local infrastructure while identity, data, release state, approval scope, and decision authority remain mission-separated.
Shared — governed memory, evidence lineage, monitoring, orchestration, local inference, and human review.
Separated — identity, data access, release state, approval scope, and decision authority.
Evidence continuity informs assurance without silently becoming operational truth.

elements.text: Working evidence, not product theater
The project can support a bounded prepared-host evaluation today while keeping broader corpus, response-route, and deployment closure explicit.
Working surfaces — Threat Matrix, Global Posture, Supply Chain, QRA review, corpus views, and docked Console exist on the prepared host.
Review separation — candidate, reviewed, accepted, rejected, pending, and compliance-credit states remain distinct.
Bounded proof — dated receipts exist for selected retrieval, review, answerability, and interaction paths.
Design-partner stage — the offer is workflow evaluation, architecture review, co-design, and prepared-host technical sessions.

elements.text: Trace one representative claim together
A useful next conversation tests one real workflow from framework source through program relationship, component or supplier lineage, evidence, review state, and final human decision.
Workflow co-design — validate how assessors, engineers, suppliers, program teams, and risk owners move through one evidence thread.
Integration design — prioritize GRC, OSCAL, PLM, requirements, test, supplier, identity, and evidence-store boundaries.
Deployment planning — define prepared-host, disconnected, policy-bounded, logging, access-control, and review requirements.
